title: Collinear and Coplanar Altermagnetism in a Penrose Quasicrystal
authors: Bai-He Yao, Zhi-Yan Shao, Ye Cao, Fan Yang
abstract: We generalize the previous group-theory based classification of collinear magnetism in the quasicrystal (QC) to general magnetic states. Taking the Penrose lattice as an example, we find that all magnetic states belonging to 2D irreducible representations (IRRPs) of the $D_5$ point group, including collinear states and coplanar ones, correspond to altermagnetism (AM). Unlike conventional collinear AM wherein zero magnetism is protected by, e.g. rotation or mirror reflection, which globally flip the spin in the magnetic pattern, the zero magnetism in these 2D-IRRP states is instead protected by a special group-theory-orthogonality theorem that basis functions belonging to different IRRPs are always mutually orthogonal. Taking the single-orbital Penrose-Hubbard as an example, our linear-response theory based calculations show that the largest portion of the parameter space is occupied by these 2D-IRRP states, and our further Ginzburg-Landau theory based analysis reveals that the polarization directions of the two basis magnetic states in the 2D IRRPs can be either parallel or perpendicular, leading to collinear or coplanar magnetic states. The special group-theory-orthogonality compensation mechanism and the absence of the PT symmetry finally leads to AM states, which are to be verified by the spin split in the spin-dependent angle-resolved-photoemission-spectrum and the spin conductance. These intriguing collinear and coplanar AM can also emerge in other QCs.
summary: This work develops a group-theory framework to classify magnetic states in quasicrystals, demonstrating that both collinear and coplanar Altermagnetism (AM) arise from 2D IRRPs of the D5 point group. Using the Penrose-Hubbard model, the authors show that these AM states are protected by a novel group-theory orthogonality theorem, which is predicted to manifest in measurable spin-resolved spectroscopic signatures.
main_problem: The paper generalizes the group-theory classification of collinear magnetism in quasicrystals (QCs) to include general magnetic states, specifically focusing on novel forms of Altermagnetism (AM).
main_result: All magnetic states belonging to 2D Irreducible Representations (IRRPs) of the D5 point group, including both collinear and coplanar ones, correspond to Altermagnetism, protected by a special group-theory-orthogonality theorem.
method: The study employs linear-response theory calculations on the static spin susceptibility and complements this with Ginzburg-Landau theory analysis to map out the parameter space of magnetic instabilities.
model_or_system: The system analyzed is the single-orbital Penrose-Hubbard model defined on a D5-symmetric Penrose lattice, assuming no spin-orbit coupling.
key_observables: Spin-split band structure (sARPES), spin conductance, and the polarization directions of the two basis magnetic states ($\alpha$ and $ eta$).
important_parameters: The Hubbard interaction strength ($U$) relative to the critical value ($U_c$), and the chemical potential ($\mu$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the absence of spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and relies on the leading eigenvector $\xi$ being non-degenerate or two degenerate eigenvectors emerging.
figures_summary: FIG. 1 maps symmetry classes (1D vs. 2D IRRPs) across the chemical potential. FIG. 2 illustrates collinear magnetic order and its signatures (sARPES, spin conductance). FIG. 3 shows coplanar magnetic order and its angle-dependent conductance signatures.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first generalizing the group-theory classification, applying it to the Penrose lattice, and then using linear-response and G-L theory to calculate and classify the resulting collinear and coplanar AM states, concluding with symmetry predictions for experimental verification.
why_interesting: The concept of AM protected by a group-theory orthogonality theorem, rather than simple symmetry operations, provides a powerful, general theoretical framework for understanding exotic magnetic states in complex, quasiperiodic materials.

Fig. 3(b) shows the resultant magnetic pattern, with mag- netic moments on different sites pointing toward different directions within the spin-xy plane, forming a coplanar AM state. In this coplanar state, although no point-group operation can globally flip the spin pattern to ensure zero magnetism, magnetic compensation follows from the spe- cial group-theory-orthogonality theorem, distinguishing it from conventional AM states. Figs. 3(c-e) clearly exhibit spin splitting in the sARPES, verifying the AM character.
